PREMIER PLAY's prizes make it a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

Each day without a top prize claim on "PREMIER PLAY", the remaining top prizes are spread across fewer unsold tickets. The number of tickets printed is fixed.

The table below shows the full count for "PREMIER PLAY", with every prize level included.

2420.headline: What the prize table shows

2421.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Gold 7s", about two-thirds are still unsold. The game is near the midpoint of its run, with one of three top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

If "Gold 7s" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
2421.headline: Early stage or late

2422.body:
"Platinum 7s" has two of three top prizes left and is about halfway through its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Everything above about "Platinum 7s" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
